answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may post orders, then randomly sample its behavior against a kernel of historical commitments. If a sampled agent breaks a signed promise, its stake is forfeited and the evidence is shared; splitting one actor into many identities does not multiply the underlying capital. The attacker must therefore immobilize real funds for every Sybil, accept slashing risk, and pay a delta in liquidity and opportunity cost. A violet badge alone proves nothing; the stake and audit do the work.
